_comment: GitHub App manifest for `policy-check-reader` — the one credential that can read
develop's branch protection. Rationale, scope, rotation and the owner-run
`hook_attributes.url` and `redirect_url` fill the manifest's webhook-config and
OAuth slots. Nothing here uses them: `default_events` is empty (no webhooks) and
there is no OAuth flow. They point at this repo's issue URL rather than inventing
live endpoints. Leave them as they are.
UNVERIFIED until the App is actually created: whether the manifest endpoint
accepts the unused `_comment` key, and whether it requires these two slots at
all. Neither has been exercised, because creating the App is an owner action.
If GitHub's form complains, drop `_comment` (this file is documented in
docs/ops/policy-check-credential.md) and read whatever the form marks required.
One permission, on purpose. `administration: read` is the minimum the
branch-protection endpoint accepts and is exactly what a workflow's own
GITHUB_TOKEN can never hold. Two installations on this org already hold it
(`cursor`, `graphite-app`), so the grant is demonstrably available.
If this credential ever needs a write, that is a new issue and a new decision.
name: policy-check-reader
